assertions.name: A5_no_distance_decay_is_structural
assertions.source: closure invariance: four routings and two axial distances agree to 1e-15, so separation is invisible to the functional

assertions.name: A6_saturation_has_the_opposite_ordering
assertions.source: model pn >> pp = nn; measured pp > pn > nn

description: Measures the load-bearing assumption that spectral_gap_bond_decay_probe (bean qou-brng) explicitly flagged as unmeasured: that a bond at separation s enters the binding functional with weight r^(s-1). It does not. Building the separation-2 bond as an actual braid word — the BKL band generator — in four independent routings (both conjugation directions, and routed from the other side), all carrying the (2,6) transposition, gives L = 0.676821592386 every time, spread 5.6e-16, and that is EXACTLY the adjacent bond's value to 7.8e-16. So the measured weight at s = 2 is 1, not r: the model would apply 0.81165 for pp/nn (19% low) and 0.99986 for pn (harmless). The reason is structural — the Markov trace is a link invariant, a function of the closure rather than the braid word, and axial separation is not a property of the closure, so no r^(s-1) weight can arise from it for any r. The sibling's RATES are untouched and verified here (1/q^2 for pp and nn to 1.15e-41); only the form is refuted. Consequence: the 3He improvement to +0.136% cannot be mechanistic. What is present instead is saturation — marginal contribution 0.659916 (far pp), 0.640829 (far pn), 0.625186 (far nn) — a function of what else is switched on, not of separation, and ordered opposite to the model's pn >> pp = nn.
caveats: THIS TOUCHES THE FORM, NOT THE RATES. The sibling's spectral gaps are exact and are re-derived here rather than quoted; 1/q^2 for pp and nn holds to 1.15e-41. The probe being addressed had already identified the form as its load-bearing assumption and said so plainly — this is the measurement it said was missing, not a correction of something it got wrong.

THE LINK-INVARIANCE ARGUMENT IS THE LIKELY MECHANISM, NOT A PROOF GIVEN HERE. What is measured is that four routings and two axial distances give one value to 1e-15. That the closures are actually isotopic is the natural explanation and is consistent with the adjacent bond (permutation [2,3]) matching the far one (permutation [2,6]), but no isotopy is exhibited and no independent link invariant is computed. If some other functional in the framework is NOT a closure invariant, a distance decay could live there and nothing here would see it.

The saturation values are quoted from all_pairs_bonds_and_saturation_probe rather than recomputed. They were measured at A = 3 only, one far-bond configuration per nucleus, so the claim that they have no r^(s-1) shape rests on the shape being wrong at the one separation available (s = 2), not on a fit across several.
